meta.project: Multilingual and Explainable ESG Intelligence Framework
meta.description: A machine-persistable reference mapping linking integrated research layers to curated literature evidence, establishing causal traceability from technical contributions to empirical foundations.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Improving Zero-shot Cross-lingual Transfer between Closely Related Languages by injecting Character-level Noise
literature_references.relevance: Provides empirical evidence for C3 and RQ1.1 by demonstrating that character-level noise improves zero-shot transfer for related language varieties, essential for Indonesian-English ESG coverage.

literature_references.title: Morphosyntactic Tagging with Pre-trained Language Models for Arabic and its Dialects
literature_references.authors: Go Inoue, Salam Khalifa, Nizar Habash
literature_references.relevance: Supports RQ1.3 by establishing that strategic fine-tuning with high-resource data from other dialects benefits low-resource regional calibration in bilingual engines.

literature_references.title: Data Augmentation and Learned Layer Aggregation for Improved Multilingual Language Understanding in Dialogue
literature_references.authors: E. Razumovskaia, Ivan Vulic, A. Korhonen
literature_references.relevance: Validates the use of layer aggregation to strengthen cross-lingual capabilities in zero-shot scenarios, supporting C1 and C3.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: Cutting Down on Prompts and Parameters: Simple Few-Shot Learning with Language Models
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C16 and RQ2.1 by proving that few-shot learning with minimal parameter updates outperforms standard fine-tuning in low-resource settings.

literature_references.title: Learning to Robustly Aggregate Labeling Functions for Semi-supervised Data Programming
literature_references.relevance: Provides the algorithmic foundation for C16 by reweighting contributions of noisy labeling functions in semi-supervised training paradigms.

literature_references.title: Disentangling the Roles of Representation and Selection in Data Pruning
literature_references.relevance: Justifies the systematic benchmarking approach in C8 by analyzing how data representation quality influences subset selection for scaling model training.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: Fact-Tree Reasoning for N-ary Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs
literature_references.relevance: Establishes the logic for C7 and RQ3.2, demonstrating how upgrading to tree-structured fact reasoning improves interpretability in graph scenarios.

literature_references.title: XPrompt: Explaining Large Language Model's Generation via Joint Prompt Attribution
literature_references.relevance: Supports C15 and RQ3.2 by providing a counterfactual framework to explain how combinatorial prompt inputs collaboratively influence model generation.

literature_references.title: STRICTA: Structured Reasoning in Critical Text Assessment for Peer Review and Beyond
literature_references.relevance: Provides a specification framework to model text assessment as an explicit, step-wise reasoning process, directly operationalizing RQ3.1.

research_questions: RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?
RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?

literature_references.title: Training Dynamics for Text Summarization Models
literature_references.relevance: Analyzes factual errors and hallucinations in later training stages, providing a theoretical base for greenwashing detection in RQ4.5.

literature_references.title: InvestAlign: Overcoming Data Scarcity in Aligning Large Language Models with Investor Decision-Making Processes Under Herd Behavior
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C11 by leveraging theoretical solutions to align LLMs with behavioral patterns in investment contexts.

literature_references.title: Input-specific Attention Subnetworks for Adversarial Detection
literature_references.relevance: Supports RQ4.1 and C14 by extracting attention-based features to discriminate between authentic and deceptive (adversarial) inputs.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: Towards Transparent Interactive Semantic Parsing via Step-by-Step Correction
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports the interactive dashboard goals of C12 and RQ5.1 by introducing a step-by-step correction framework for users.

literature_references.title: EducationQ: Evaluating LLMs' Teaching Capabilities Through Multi-Agent Dialogue Framework
literature_references.relevance: Justifies the multi-agent architecture in Objective 5 by proposing a framework for efficient assessment through specialized agents in dynamic scenarios.

literature_references.title: Training Text-to-Text Transformers with Privacy Guarantees
literature_references.relevance: Supports the deployment criteria of C1 by addressing privacy concerns in text-to-text models release to the public.
